- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model frequently underreacts to sharp price spikes in the prior 3–5 days; add a small lagged momentum boost to forecast.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after a spike), model often holds too high; apply downward bias in next period.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive — cap early forecast peaks.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the rebound — anticipate a 1–2 day lagged recovery.
- When true price exceeds forecast by >5% in 3–5 days, model is likely underestimating sentiment-driven momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.
